title: Louisville adult bands and the Lloyd Scott trombonists
summary: Local bands included Winstead's Wonders, Howard Jordan's and Furman Tapp's; Dickie Wells, Bill Coleman and Frankie Newton were in Lloyd Scott's band, and his brother-in-law Russell Bowles took Dickie's place with Tapp.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And it was a lot of older guys around there playing, you know. Winstead's Wonders, they called them, about seven or eight pieces, and Howard Jordan's band. He had about 7, or maybe about 10. And Tapp, this guy I was telling you, Furman Tapp, he' had about eight. That's who my brother-in-law played the trombone with. Because Dickie had gone, and he was playing with Tapp for awhile, and they come through and went with Lloyd Scott, and that was Dickie, and Bill Coleman.
And Frankie Newton. Yeah. All them was in that band together, with Lloyd Scott.
Yeah, they went there. And then my brother-in-law, my wife's brother, Russell Bowles, played with Lunsford in later years.
You might remember him. And he --
Yeah. He took Dickie's place with Tapp. And finally he left.
